rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis specifies the same intervention as the target: DLP-printed green bodies debound under oxygen-rich ambient air or oxygen-deficient mechanical-pump evacuation, followed by solid-state sintering at 800, 1000, 1050, or 1100 °C for 24 h with the same debinding holds. All specifics match exactly.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis lists the same printing parameters (405 nm, 19.57 mW/cm², 100 s exposure, 70 μm layers, 20 layers), ultrasonic cleaning, atmosphere-dependent debinding, furnace sintering over 800–1100 °C, and exclusion of the 600 °C sample. All conditions are identical.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis describes the same dual-pathway mechanism: oxygen-rich debinding causing CO/CO2-driven cracking and oxide barriers that delay densification, while oxygen-deficient debinding retains carbon, reduces porosity, and facilitates diffusion and bonding at lower temperatures. The structural mediators (retained carbon, oxide layers, pore volume, cracking) are identical.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts earlier densification and comparable maximum compressive strength at a 50 °C lower sintering temperature under oxygen-deficient debinding, matching the target's reported result of ~5.1 MPa at 1050 °C vs. 1100 °C for oxygen-rich conditions.
